body.statement: Let \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{uv})_{1\le u\le S,\,1\le v\le T})\).  Under \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}, fix a law \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), a cohort \(s\), a unit \(i\), an event \(E\in\mathcal X\), and a constant \(b\ne0\).  If \(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=b\mathbf 1_E\) almost surely conditional on \(z_0\), then \(\Pr_P(E\mid z_0)\in\{0,1\}\).  Consequently, in the former scalar common-design-shock construction with \(X_{11}\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), \(E=\{X_{11}\le q\}\), \(q\in(0,1)\), and \(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=b_*\mathbf 1_E\) for \(b_*>0\), the shocked law violates \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} and is not in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\).  Thus the former two-law obstruction is excluded from the repaired class.
body.justification: This lemma pinpoints the observed-law restriction that invalidates the former common-design-shock counterexample.
body.gap: It is an exclusion audit for one obsolete witness, not a minimax lower bound for the repaired model.
body.consumer: The repaired-class supporting theorem uses it to separate sampling centering from causal event-date transport.
body.proof_tex:
Let
\[
 \mathcal X=\sigma\!\left((X_{uv})_{1\le u\le S,\,1\le v\le T}\right),
 \qquad
 p_E=\Pr_P(E\mid z_0),
 \qquad
 \mu_{si}=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].
\]
Membership of \(P\) in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), \texttt{def:panel-model-class}, \texttt{ass:bounded-wealth}, and \texttt{ass:consistency} imply that \(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) is integrable.  Since \(E\in\mathcal X\), the random variable \(b\mathbf 1_E\) is measurable with respect to \(\sigma(z_0,\mathcal X)\).  The assumed equality \(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=b\mathbf 1_E\), valid almost surely under the conditional law given \(z_0\), therefore implies
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =b\mathbf 1_E
 \quad\text{almost surely under that conditional law}.                                      \tag{1}
\]
On the other hand, \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]
 =\mu_{si}
 \quad\text{almost surely}.                                                                  \tag{2}
\]
Taking conditional expectation given \(z_0\) in the assumed shock representation gives
\[
 \mu_{si}=b\,\mathbb E_P[\mathbf 1_E\mid z_0]=bp_E.                                           \tag{3}
\]
Combining (1)--(3), squaring, and taking conditional expectation given \(z_0\) yields
\[
 0
 =\mathbb E_P[(b\mathbf 1_E-bp_E)^2\mid z_0]
 =b^2\mathbb E_P[(\mathbf 1_E-p_E)^2\mid z_0]
 =b^2p_E(1-p_E).                                                                              \tag{4}
\]
The last equality uses \(\mathbf 1_E^2=\mathbf 1_E\) and \(\mathbb E_P[\mathbf 1_E\mid z_0]=p_E\).  Because \(b\ne0\), division by \(b^2\) in (4) gives \(p_E(1-p_E)=0\).  Since a conditional probability lies in \([0,1]\),
\[
 \Pr_P(E\mid z_0)=p_E\in\{0,1\}.
\]

For the former scalar construction in the statement, \(z_0\) is fixed, \(X_{11}\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), \(E=\{X_{11}\le q\}\), and \(q\in(0,1)\).  Hence
\[
 \Pr_P(E\mid z_0)=\Pr_P(X_{11}\le q\mid z_0)=q\in(0,1).
\]
Taking \(b=b_*>0\) contradicts (4).  Thus the shocked law violates \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}; by the member-property construction in \texttt{def:panel-model-class}, it is not an element of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\).  The former obstruction required the shocked law to belong to that class, so that obstruction is excluded.  This argument uses the observed-law centering restriction and does not invoke causal event-date transport.
